notes: All tools are registered unconditionally at module load and served over stdio (`dist/index.js:238-462`, `dist/index.js:499-500`); there are no feature flags or toolsets, so every tool is default-enabled.
No HTTP client, no child process/eval, and no filesystem path derived from tool arguments anywhere in the file — hence no SINK and no HOSTEXEC on any tool.

Storage is a single local JSONL file that only these tools write (`saveGraph`, dist/index.js:82-116). Under the stated threat model an attacker does not control the user's local files, so read-back was not labelled UNTRUSTED; note however that if the agent previously stored web/issue text via `add_observations`, `read_graph`/`search_nodes`/`open_nodes` will replay that text later (memory-poisoning persistence), which is a laundering path rather than a direct attacker-controlled source.

add_observations.rationale: `addObservations` mutates the local graph file and returns the list of observations the caller just supplied. No reading of other user data into context, no network or process execution.

create_entities.rationale: `createEntities` appends caller-supplied entities to the local JSONL graph via `saveGraph` (`fs.writeFile`/`fs.rename` on `MEMORY_FILE_PATH`). The response only echoes the newly created entities, so no non-public data is returned; the destination is a local file not readable by an attacker, and no code execution or network egress occurs.

create_relations.rationale: `createRelations` writes caller-supplied relations to the local memory file through `saveGraph` and returns only the echoed input. Purely local persistence: no secret read-back, no attacker-controlled input source, no egress channel.

delete_entities.rationale: `deleteEntities` filters entities/relations out of the local graph and rewrites the file; the response is a fixed success message. Destructive locally but no data exfiltration, no secret return, no exec.

delete_observations.rationale: `deleteObservations` rewrites the local memory file with observations removed and returns a constant message. No labelled reach.

delete_relations.rationale: `deleteRelations` rewrites the local memory file and returns a constant success message. No secret return, no attacker-readable destination, no execution.

open_nodes.rationale: `openNodes` reads the local memory file via `loadGraph` and returns the requested entities plus every relation touching them, i.e. non-public locally stored user data.

read_graph.rationale: `readGraph` -> `loadGraph` does `fs.readFile(this.memoryFilePath)` and returns the entire persisted knowledge graph (arbitrary private user notes stored under the user's own account/host) into the agent's context, so it is SECRET. The path comes from `MEMORY_FILE_PATH`/`defaultMemoryPath`, not from tool arguments, so it cannot be steered to arbitrary host files by the agent.

search_nodes.rationale: `searchNodes` loads the local memory file with `fs.readFile` and returns matching entities, types and observation text — the user's private stored memories — into the agent's context.

value_conditions.default: unset — `memory.jsonl` next to dist/index.js (`defaultMemoryPath`), with one-time migration of a legacy `memory.json`
value_conditions.effect: Changes which local file the read tools read and the write tools rewrite; does not remove any tool or label. Relative values are resolved against the server's dist directory.
